bets.name: Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer
bets.thesis: Make Takeda's own trial, real-world, assay and plasma data reusable under one governed layer so that a small number of named decisions (target choice, trial design, supply planning) can be measured against a pre-agreed baseline. (RECOMMENDATION, conditional on IVB-001.)
bets.market_change: Competitors are building proprietary data assets and opening them internally: AbbVie ARCH holds 124 TB and opened de-identified data from 2,000+ trials to all R&D; Lilly TuneLab rests on data Lilly estimates cost over USD 1bn [CLM-006032] [CLM-006034] [CLM-000280]. Compute and third-party models are purchasable by rivals, so proprietary data is the one defensible input [CLM-006055]. (INTERPRETATION)
bets.problem: Takeda's public record shows a platform and an aspiration but no quantified AI or data outcome [CLM-006045] [CLM-011053]. Without an inventory of products, users and outcomes, spending cannot be linked to value (IVB-001). Whether Takeda's data estate is fragmented as AbbVie's was is unknown (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011055].
bets.baseline_detail: Class 9, enterprise data and AI platform: a Databricks-hosted agent platform for 10,000+ employees exists, outcomes unproven [CLM-005058] [CLM-005080]. Maturity must be assessed first (IVB-001), so this bet extends and governs an existing platform; it does not start a new one.
bets.moat_explanation: Data and learning: decision-linked data that is costly to regenerate improves each later model and trial design; workflow integration comes from embedding the layer in named decisions. It compounds only if each decision is logged against a baseline so the layer learns from outcomes (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011082].

build: Governance, data catalogue, decision log and metrics on the existing platform
Reuse policy for de-identified trial and real-world data
license: Commodity data tooling from the existing Databricks relationship [CLM-005058]

time_to_value.near_term: 12-24 months: production inventory, 2-3 decisions with baselines (closes IVB-001).
time_to_value.long_horizon: 2030-2035: model-informed target and trial-design decisions with measured cycle-time or hit-rate effect; 2035-2040: compounding only if measured.

outcomes: Inventory of data and AI products in production with owner, users, baseline and measured benefit
Named decisions where a model changed the outcome versus a pre-agreed baseline
Share of trial data reusable across franchises

risks.text: Estate may already be well governed, so the incremental value is small (IVB-001).
AI credibility documentation expectations [CLM-006046].
Usage is mistaken for value, as in competitor metrics [CLM-006022].
Platform spend without outcome evidence is hard to stop once started.

bets.strategic_options_text: Expand if two decisions show measured gains by gate 3; redirect to federated use (BET-08) if Takeda data proves too sparse; stop if no baseline can be set.
bets.decision_rationale: Small, ring-fenced and a prerequisite for stage-3 automation and for judging AI partnerships; the maturity assessment (IVB-001) gates the follow-on.
v2_changes: (decision record row 7) Roadmap: RM-015 (decision log gate) is now a wired prerequisite of RM-020 (BET-07 stop-or-expand). Size unchanged.
bets.sequencing: Start with a thin slice (metadata standards and decision log) in H1 2027 alongside BET-09; the full layer is a hard prerequisite for any stage-3 closed-loop pilot (HYPOTHESIS). Argument: AbbVie built ARCH with fewer than ten staff [CLM-006032], so the data layer costs little relative to running automation without it; Zymergen paired automation and ML and still failed commercially [CLM-006051].
evidence: FACT: ARCH was built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors; a governance decision opened trial data to all R&D [CLM-006032] [CLM-006034]. Outcome evidence is a preprint not opened by A6.
FACT: across ARCH, TuneLab, Polyphonic and the AISB model, none has independent outcome evidence [CLM-011052] [CLM-006054 as corrected by the audit: wording stronger than sources support].
FACT: Takeda reports 63.4% of workforce using gen-AI tools; this is a usage measure, as are J&J's course completions and unbaselined enrolment multiple [CLM-014043] [CLM-006022] [CLM-006020].
HYPOTHESIS: one governed layer raises reuse of Takeda's own trial and real-world data if the estate is fragmented [CLM-011055].

FACT (risk): FDA's January 2025 draft guidance proposes risk-based credibility for AI used in regulatory decisions, so model evidence must be documented [CLM-006046]; Takeda's own 20-F warns models may be flawed or trained on inadequate data [CLM-005054].

confidence_detail.known: Platform exists; competitors' data layers exist; no outcomes anywhere [CLM-005058] [CLM-011052].
confidence_detail.assumed: Cost and fragmentation level (ASM-101); that decisions can be baselined.

bets.name: Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme
bets.thesis: Test whether donor, yield and process data from the plasma network are a proprietary data class (no plasma peer is in the comparison set, so uniqueness is untested) by funding only a baseline, a demand-versus-capacity test, a plasma-peer benchmark and a one-site shadow-mode tranche before any fixed-price automation or network roll-out. (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011056] [CLM-011031]
bets.market_change: Plasma-derived therapies sit outside the biosimilar mechanism that threatens Entyvio; immunoglobulins were JPY 790.6bn (18% of FY2025 revenue) with PDT revenue +8.5% AER in H1 FY2026 (-1.5% CER), which does not show that capacity rather than demand binds [CLM-005064]. Lilly's record shows capacity bound a blockbuster until 2024, but that is an obesity-drug analogue, not plasma [CLM-001066] [CLM-000172]. (INTERPRETATION)
bets.problem: Whether plasma is a platform strength or only a large business depends on yield per centre and cost per litre, which are not public (IVB-006). Automation in GMP settings carries validation burden and Takeda has one documented warning letter and supply shortage [CLM-005020].
bets.baseline_detail: Class 2, plasma network and PDT manufacturing: 233 to 275 centres (FY2022-FY2024), 270+ with adaptive nomograms, 99.6% on-time in-full, USD 230m Los Angeles fractionation expansion; yield and cost per litre are not public (IVB-006) [CLM-005063] [CLM-005060] [CLM-014046] [CLM-005065]. Class 12 manufacturing quality is EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED after the Hikari warning letter [CLM-005020]. This bet builds on a strength; it must first measure headroom.
bets.moat_explanation: Infrastructure and data: fractionation capacity takes years to copy and process data compounds with each batch; learning if yield models are retrained on every lot. Regulatory experience is the support layer: automated steps must be validated, which is slow for rivals and for Takeda (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011085] [CLM-011039].

build: Process-data capture and yield models
Single-site (Los Angeles) pilot design and acceptance criteria
license: Nomogram and donor-tool vendors already used [CLM-005060]
partner: Automation vendors on fixed-price, outcome-linked terms [CLM-011031]

time_to_value.near_term: 2027-2029: yield and cost-per-litre baseline, demand-versus-capacity test, plasma-peer benchmark and a one-site shadow-mode run; remainder released only if all pass.
time_to_value.long_horizon: 2030-2035: network roll-out if headroom is shown; 2035-2040: possible neutral analytics offer (low confidence).

outcomes: Yield per litre of plasma, deviation rate and cost per litre before and after pilot (company-defined)
On-time in-full held at or above FY2025 99.6% [CLM-014046]
Inspection record without new observations
Demand-versus-capacity test result (is plasma demand- or capacity-bound?)
Plasma-peer benchmark of yield and cost per litre against the ASM-031 threshold re-based on money

risks.text: GMP validation of automated steps; prior warning letter [CLM-005020].
Vendor fixed-price terms may not be available at plant complexity.
Donor data capture may be inconsistent across centres (IVB-006).
Incremental to the base USD 230m expansion; double-counting risk [CLM-005065].
Plasma peers' data position is unbenchmarked; the uniqueness claim may fail [CLM-011056] [CLM-009091].
Demand-bound, not capacity-bound, would remove the case for automation capex [CLM-005064].

bets.strategic_options_text: Expand to a pilot only if the baseline shows headroom and demand is capacity-bound; redirect to other core uses if demand-bound; stop if headroom is below the re-based ASM-031 threshold.
bets.decision_rationale: Cheap baseline and shadow-mode tranche produces the data the council says is missing; the remainder of the programme is contingent on the demand-versus-capacity test, the plasma-peer benchmark and ASM-031 re-based on money (value of a gain per litre against pilot and run cost). Takeda-execution council dissent recorded: it supports BUILD because the CEO led the PDT unit and the network runs 270+ centres at 99.6% on-time in-full [CLM-005074] [CLM-005063] [CLM-014046]. The red team's call to reject any plasma spend is not accepted.
v2_changes: (decision record row 4) BUILD -> EXPERIMENT; balanced USD 430m -> 230m (baseline and shadow-mode tranche about USD 65m at risk, remainder contingent); ASM-031 re-based on money; demand-versus-capacity and plasma-peer tests added as gates; Takeda-execution council dissent recorded.
bets.sequencing: Baseline and shadow-mode tranche first (about USD 65m at risk in the first two gates, ASSUMPTION ASM-102); the pilot, roll-out and neutral-analytics decision are contingent. Nomogram and process data already exist at site level [CLM-005060], so the tranche does not wait for BET-01; soft dependency on BET-01 standards from 2028.
evidence: FACT: nomogram programmes rolled out across 270+ centres; AI-powered donor tools reported in FY2025 [CLM-005060] [CLM-014046]; 170+ predictive-maintenance agents at Lessines with expansion planned by 2027 (company-reported, no outcome) [CLM-014041].

FACT: NASA documents record Falcon 9 development at about USD 390m against model estimates of USD 1.7-4.0bn under fixed-price contracts, but the cause of the gap is not isolated and each cargo partner suffered catastrophic failures [CLM-011005] [CLM-011006] [CLM-011008]. Analogy only.

FACT (counter-evidence): no public evidence of Takeda lab, continuous-manufacturing or manufacturing robotics [CLM-005067]; Lilly's Lebanon robotics were seen on a tour with no performance data [CLM-006002]; Medicine Foundry (USD 4.5bn) is concept [CLM-006000] [CLM-006001].
HYPOTHESIS: a neutral-capacity or shared-analytics role could follow if spare capacity exists; sponsors guard process and liability [CLM-011041] [CLM-011040].
FACT: PDT revenue was -1.5% at constant rates in H1 FY2026, so the public record does not show a capacity constraint; a demand-versus-capacity test is a gate [CLM-005064].
INTERPRETATION: 'no competitor holds this data' holds only because the comparison set has no plasma peer; the registry holds none, so a plasma-peer benchmark is a gate [CLM-011056] [CLM-009091].
FACT (counter-evidence): fixed-price vendor terms are a NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH hypothesis and there is no fixed-price vendor evidence for plasma plants [CLM-011031].

confidence_detail.known: Network scale, capacity expansion, on-time in-full [CLM-005063] [CLM-005065] [CLM-014046].
confidence_detail.assumed: Yield and cost headroom (ASM-031); cost of upgrades (ASM-102).

bets.name: Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform
bets.thesis: Run orexin biology as a platform with a second differentiated asset, funded at the constrained discovery size, with a Phase 1 gate before the H2 tranche, an additionality test against base R&D and a competitor orexin scan. (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011038]
bets.market_change: A platform does not protect a single product (Regeneron EYLEA net sales -42% in 2025), so the value of a platform is repeated assets (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011017] [CLM-011037]. Neuroscience and psychiatry is the common failure site of the window across AbbVie, J&J and Takeda [CLM-003054] [CLM-002039] [CLM-012120].
bets.problem: After 2030 the six late-stage programmes carry the pipeline; refill depends on early depth that is not public (IVB-008). TAK-994 was stopped for liver safety, so a second asset is not assured [CLM-005023].
bets.baseline_detail: Class 3, rare disease and orexin science: oveporexton discovered in Shonan, FDA-approved 2026-08-05; Takeda calls itself world leader in orexin science [CLM-005048] [CLM-012149]. Pipeline refill beyond the six late-stage programmes is unknown (IVB-008) [CLM-005044].
bets.moat_explanation: IP and learning: disease-biology depth is slow to buy and each asset's clinical data sharpens the next; regulatory experience from a first approval lowers review risk for follow-ons. Compounding requires a second asset and is unproven (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011036].

build: Discovery and early clinical team in Shonan with a multi-asset plan
license: Tools and models for design as needed

time_to_value.long_horizon: 2032-2037: second asset in late-stage development; 2038-2040: platform proof only if two assets approve.

outcomes: Number of orexin-class clinical candidates and indications
Phase 1 to Phase 2 transition rate versus conventional programmes
Second-asset first-in-human by about 2030 (ASSUMPTION)
Additionality result: share of the bet's spend that is incremental to base R&D (test design set at the feasibility gate)
Competitor orexin scan completed before the H2 tranche

risks.text: Orexin success may not generalise; liver safety history [CLM-005023].
Competitor orexin programmes are not in the registry (research gap, logged in evidence_gaps.md).
Long-dated and exposed in a downturn.

bets.strategic_options_text: Expand on a clean second-asset Phase 1; partner out indications outside Takeda's depth; stop at gate 2 if no candidate beats a safety criterion.
bets.decision_rationale: Builds on a proven in-house capability, sized at the constrained discovery size (v1 balanced was larger). The Phase 1 gate (second candidate clean through Phase 1, RM-030, target 2030 H1) releases the H2 tranche; an additionality test against base R&D and a competitor scan precede it. Removing BET-03 entirely is not accepted: orexin is Takeda's only evidenced in-house discovery success in the window [CLM-009076] [CLM-005048].
v2_changes: (decision record row 5) Balanced USD 500m -> 300m; Phase 1 gate before the H2 tranche (RM-030); additionality test against base R&D and competitor orexin scan added (new RM-052).
bets.sequencing: Independent of BET-01 data layer; benefits from BET-07 design tools. Start in H1 (discovery to second-asset readiness takes years, INTERPRETATION); H2 tranche only after the Phase 1 gate and the additionality test.
evidence: FACT: oveporexton approved 2026-08-05 from in-house discovery; efficacy statements are company-reported [CLM-012149] [CLM-005048].
FACT: TAK-994 stopped (liver-related signal); soticlestat Phase 3 missed (June 2024), JPY 21.5bn impairment [CLM-012119] [CLM-012120] [CLM-009083].
FACT (analogue): Regeneron built VelociSuite and a genetics centre with over 3 million samples; contribution to approvals is not quantified [CLM-011015] [CLM-011016].

INTERPRETATION: the lesson from AbbVie, J&J and Takeda is to gate CNS assets on Phase 2 quality and placebo response, and not to infer that orexin success transfers to other CNS bets [CLM-003057] [CLM-012135].
INTERPRETATION: the orexin discovery team already sits in base R&D (JPY 675.9bn), so the incrementality of the spend cannot be tested without an additionality test [CLM-005004] [CLM-005048].
FACT (research gap): competitor orexin programmes are not in the registry; a competitor scan is a gate [CLM-005029].

confidence_detail.assumed: That a credible second asset exists (ASM-021, ASM-103).

bets.name: Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle
bets.thesis: Build payer-contracting and formulary-defence depth, outcomes evidence and lifecycle plans for Entyvio ahead of Medicare negotiation (January 2028) and biosimilar entry, to delay erosion and measure it. The outcome is 'delay and measure', not 'retain revenue': the January 2028 price is statutory and PBM private-label biosimilars route around contracts. (RECOMMENDATION) [CLM-011072] [CLM-007026] [CLM-007015]
bets.market_change: Entyvio loses regulatory exclusivity in the latter half of the decade, some patents expire in 2032 with revocation actions filed, two biosimilar BLAs are under FDA review, and Entyvio is selected for Medicare negotiation from January 2028 [CLM-005017] [CLM-014050] [CLM-014051] [CLM-007026]. PBM template changes decide outcomes: from 1 July 2026 CVS template formularies prefer interchangeable Stelara biosimilars [CLM-007015], and Takeda's 20-F says rebate details are undisclosed and formulary exclusion can directly reduce usage [CLM-007025].
bets.problem: Entyvio is the largest single exposure and Takeda's contracting depth is unknown. Humira lost 78.6% in three years even with rebate-for-access contracts and a co-brand route, and U.S. Humira fell 41% in 2024 and 57% in 2025 [CLM-003002] [CLM-003007] [CLM-003010] [CLM-007016].
bets.baseline_detail: Class 1 GI and immunology is a strength (Entyvio JPY 958.0bn, 21% of revenue) but class 14 patient services and market access is an EVIDENCE_GAP (no public rebate or contracting data) and class 7 LOE replacement is EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED [CLM-005009] [CLM-005072] [CLM-005017]. Takeda already runs the SC pen and pediatric labels [CLM-005018]; the gap is payer defence, not product.
bets.moat_explanation: Workflow integration (formulary position, patient hub and SC pen use) and IP posture. Both are removable (PBM template change, patent revocation), so this is defence, not a compounding moat (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011086] [CLM-007015].

build: Payer analytics and contracting team capability
Entyvio real-world evidence and persistence study plan
partner: Specialty distribution and PBM contracting partners as needed

time_to_value.near_term: 2027 H1: benefit-channel gate (RM-003). 2028 H1: contracting posture ready for the January 2028 negotiated price and the biosimilar-event playbook live (RM-026, moved up from 2029 H2).
time_to_value.long_horizon: 2030-2034: biosimilar-event playbook; value measured as net revenue retained versus ASM-024 erosion.

outcomes: Entyvio net price and persistence measured against the ASM-024 low case after the 2028 negotiation and any biosimilar entry (measured, not forecast)
Benefit-channel split (medical versus pharmacy) known by 2027 H1 (IVB-004) and spend redirected if most volume is outside the contractable channel
SC share of Entyvio patients (IVB-004)
Time-to-erosion versus the AbbVie and J&J analogues

risks.text: Biosimilar or PBM private-label entry on a timetable Takeda does not control [CLM-014051].
Medicare negotiation and Part D redesign [CLM-007026].
Contracting capability is an EVIDENCE_GAP [CLM-005072].
Patient-programme redesign without a pilot cost AbbVie share [CLM-003033] [CLM-003088].
If most Entyvio volume sits outside the contractable pharmacy channel, contracting spend is misdirected (benefit-channel gate, RM-003).

bets.strategic_options_text: Expand to settlement-style IP posture if litigation allows; redirect spend to lifecycle if erosion is slower; no divest or stop option before 2032.
bets.decision_rationale: Largest exposure, best-evidenced transferable mechanisms (LES-05, LES-14, LES-21); low capital relative to revenue at risk. v2: stays BUILD, with a hard benefit-channel gate at 2027 H1 and the outcome reframed to delay and measure because Humira held at least 97% of volume yet lost 78.6% in three years [CLM-003007] [CLM-003002].
v2_changes: (decision record row 6) Stays BUILD; benefit-channel gate at 2027 H1 (RM-003, IVB-004) with redirect rule; outcome reframed from 'retain 10 points of erosion' to 'delay and measure'; playbook RM-026 moved to 2028 H1 (row 2).
(decision record row 10) Evidence_backed -> hypothesis; CVS Zepbound removal text corrected from about 11 months [CLM-007011] to about 15 months [CLM-007013].
bets.sequencing: Time-boxed by dated external events: benefit-channel gate 2027 H1, January 2028 negotiation [CLM-007026], playbook live 2028 H1 (early-entry stress case), biosimilar BLA reviews [CLM-014051], 2032 patents [CLM-005017]. If the benefit-channel gate shows most volume outside the contractable pharmacy channel, redirect part of the balanced total to provider and site-of-care strategy. Cannot be postponed.
evidence: FACT: AbbVie kept at least 97% of volume to March 2024 through rebate-for-access, then supplied a co-branded Humira to CVS Cordavis after the April 2024 formulary change [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008] [CLM-003009].
FACT: AbbVie's settlements put Rinvoq generic entry not before April 2037, four years after the 2033 composition patent [CLM-003021] [CLM-003087].

FACT: Lilly realised prices fell 5% (Q4 2025) and 15% (Q3 2026) while volume rose 46% and 53% [CLM-014003] [CLM-014004]; CVS Caremark removed Zepbound for about 15 months (1 July 2025 to restoration on 1 October 2026) [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013].
INTERPRETATION: plan for price erosion in the core franchise, not only volume loss [CLM-001003] [CLM-008022].

FACT (gap): the registry has no Entyvio medical-benefit versus pharmacy-benefit split, so the contractable share of volume is unknown; this is the benefit-channel gate (IVB-004) [CLM-005072] [CLM-007016].

confidence_detail.known: Dates, concentration and competitor mechanisms [CLM-005017] [CLM-007026] [CLM-003007]; load-bearing recommendation claim CLM-011072 is not fully supported, so the label is hypothesis.
confidence_detail.assumed: Erosion curve and entry date (ASM-024, ASM-025); programme cost (ASM-104).

bets.name: Zasocitinib breadth and immunology successor evidence
bets.thesis: Extend zasocitinib across indications and with comparative data before the Entyvio cliff, copying the AbbVie pattern of indication breadth plus head-to-head evidence, and decide separately whether a GI-indication successor is credible. (RECOMMENDATION, partly already in Takeda's plan.)
bets.market_change: Skyrizi plus Rinvoq rose from USD 7,687m (2022) to USD 25,866m (2025) against Humira's USD 16,697m loss because they were marketed and extended across indications before the cliff; J&J's Tremfya offset only about 35% of Stelara's loss in year one [CLM-003014] [CLM-003084] [CLM-002065].
bets.problem: Takeda's successors are not yet marketed; the USD 10-20bn peak potential for six programmes is a company statement not adjusted for probability of success [CLM-005041] [CLM-014049]. Base revenue is still falling (H1 FY2026 -1.0% CER) [CLM-005011].
bets.baseline_detail: Class 7 LOE replacement is EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED; class 4 late-stage execution is an EXISTING_STRENGTH: NDA accepted with Priority Review 2026-09-14, PsA Phase 3 running to May 2027, head-to-head win over deucravacitinib [CLM-005035] [CLM-005037] [CLM-005034]. Zasocitinib is not an Entyvio successor in gastroenterology; it replaces revenue, not the franchise (LES-07).
bets.moat_explanation: Regulatory experience and label breadth: each added indication increases the base on which a payer contract and prescriber habit can form; IP is the compound patent to be assessed internally (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-003084].

build: Incremental indication and comparative studies beyond the current plan
license: Further rights only if a GI-class gap is identified

time_to_value.near_term: 2027-2028: PsA readout (May 2027 study end) and psoriasis launch.

outcomes: Time to first prescription and payer coverage at 6 and 12 months
Indications labelled by 2032
Share of Entyvio revenue replaced (tracked, not forecast)

risks.text: Crowded psoriasis class with IL-23 and oral competitors (not researched here).
Launch timing tied to site inspection status incl. third-party sites [CLM-012134] [CLM-005029].
Class 8 launch execution is POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY [CLM-005074].
Milestones of USD 1.0bn each at USD 4bn and 5bn annual net sales [CLM-009076].

bets.strategic_options_text: Expand into additional immune indications on positive Phase 2; partner ex-US if capacity-limited; no stop before approval.
bets.decision_rationale: Mostly inside the plan; the incremental decision is breadth and comparative evidence. Marked INVEST not BUILD because the asset already exists.
v2_changes: (decision record row 10) Confidence relabelled evidence_backed -> hypothesis: a load-bearing claim is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED or NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH (CLM-011054, CLM-011065, CLM-011066, CLM-011072, CLM-011073, CLM-007053).
bets.sequencing: Time-boxed by regulatory dates and by the Entyvio timeline; must precede any BET-18 deal sizing because the replacement gap cannot be measured without launch curves (IVB-005).
